'''Amanokaguyama Shrine''' (あまのかぐやまじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Kashihara, Nara|Q496319|qid=Q496319}}. It is enshrined on the northern foothills of {{ill|Mount Amanokagu|Q11443780|qid=Q11443780}}. Together with {{ill|Uneotsutamoto Shrine|Q28685121|qid=Q28685121}}, Sakamon Shrine (Amano Iwato Shrine), and {{ill|Uneoza Taketsuyasugami Shrine|Q30931377|qid=Q30931377}}, it is collectively called the “Amanokaguyama-ni-masu Yonkasho Shrine”<ref>[https://genbu.net/data/yamato/tutamoto_title.htm Uneo Tsutamoto Shrine]</ref><ref>Washū Gogun Jinja Jinmeichō Tairyaku Chūkai</ref>.

===Enshrined deity===
* {{ill|Kushimachi no Mikoto|Q108039939|qid=Q108039939}} (くしまちのみこと)
*: A deity who governs {{ill|Futomani|Q5510530|qid=Q5510530}}.

===History===
The founding date is unknown, but ancient historical sources record the following:
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōyamato Province Tax Ledger}} (730): “One chō of sacred fields for Kushimachi, seed rice twenty bundles”
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Daidō First Year Decree}} (806): “Deity Kushimachinomikoto, one household”
* {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku}}・January 27, Jōgan 1 (859): “Bestowed Junior Fifth Rank Lower, then promoted to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (referring here to Kushimachinomikoto)”
* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} (927): “Yamato Province, Tōichi District, Amanokaguyama-ni-masu Kushimanomikoto Shrine, major shrine, monthly and Niiname offerings”
From these records, it can be said with certainty that the shrine existed in the 8th century<ref>[http://www.y-tohara.com/nara-kaguyama.html Amanokaguyama-ni-masu Kushimanomikoto Shrine (Nara, Kashihara City) – Tohara Top Page]</ref>.

===The Hahaka Tree===
The {{ill|Prunus grayana|Q2700694|qid=Q2700694|lt=hahaka tree}} found within the shrine grounds is said to have been used for divination in ancient times. The enshrined deity, Kushimachinomikoto, is a god of divination who interprets divine will, and was revered as a deity involved in turtle-shell divination used to decide matters of national importance, as well as in the divination for determining sacred rice fields for offerings performed at the {{ill|Daijosai|Q11433653|qid=Q11433653}}<ref name="Blog">[https://nihonshinwa.com/archives/870 Amanokaguyama Shrine | Enshrining the divination deity “Kushimanomikoto” who seeks divine will! Does the hahaka tree used in the Amano Iwato myth grow within the grounds? A super mythological romance spot!]</ref>. In the {{ill|Kojiki|ace|Kojiki|ar|كوجيكي|az|Kociki|bcl|Kojiki|be|Кодзікі|bg|Коджики|ca|Kojiki|ckb|کۆجیکی|cs|Kodžiki|da|Kojiki|de|Kojiki|eo|Koĝiki|es|Kojiki|et|Kojiki|eu|Kojiki|fa|کوجیکی|fi|Kojiki|fr|Kojiki|gl|Kojiki|he|קוג'יקי|hi|कोजिकी|hr|Kojiki|hu|Kodzsiki|hy|Կոձիկի|id|Kojiki|it|Kojiki|ja|古事記|ka|კოძიკი|kk|Кодзики|kn|ಕೋಜಿಕಿ|ko|고사기|la|Kojiki|lt|Kodžiki|mk|Коџики|ml|കൊജികി|ms|Kojiki|my|ခိုဂျိခိ|nl|Kojiki|no|Kojiki|oc|Kojiki|pl|Kojiki|pt|Kojiki|ro|Kojiki|rsk|Кодїки|ru|Кодзики|sh|Kojiki|simple|Kojiki|sk|Kodžiki|sl|Kodžiki|sr|Коџики|sv|Kojiki|ta|கோஜிகி|th|โคจิกิ|tl|Kojiki|tr|Kojiki|uk|Кодзікі|vi|Cổ sự ký|zh|古事記|zh_classical|古事記|qid=Q813031}}, in the {{ill|Amano-Iwato|Q3231835|qid=Q3231835|lt=Amano Iwato myth}}, it is written:

“Summoning {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Futodama-no-Mikoto}}, they pulled out the shoulder bone of a true male deer from Mount Amanokaguyama, took the hahaka of Mount Amanokaguyama, and performed divination…”

This describes how the bones of a male deer from Amanokaguyama were extracted and burned with the bark of the ‘shuzakura’ tree to divine good or ill<ref>[https://www.city.kashihara.nara.jp/kankou/own_kankou/kankou/spot/amanokaguyama.html Kashihara City / Amanokaguyama Shrine]</ref>.

===Amanokaguyama-ni-masu Kushimanomikoto Shrine===
In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is recorded as “Yamato Province, Tōichi District, Amanokaguyama-ni-masu Kushimanomikoto Shrine, major shrine, monthly and Niiname offerings,” and the prevailing theory identifies Amanokaguyama-ni-masu Kushimanomikoto Shrine with Amanokaguyama Shrine. However, there is also a theory identifying it with Kunitokotachi Shrine, which is enshrined at the summit of Mount Amanokaguyama, making this a disputed shrine identification<ref name="Blog">[https://nihonshinwa.com/archives/870 Amanokaguyama Shrine | Enshrining the divination deity “Kushimanomikoto” who seeks divine will! Does the hahaka tree used in the Amano Iwato myth grow within the grounds? A super mythological romance spot!]</ref>.
